answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a 100-token bond locked for 30 days and three independent audits before voting weight activates. Each new identity raises the bond by 25% and adds one audit round, so collusion has increasing marginal cost. Random peers verify signed task receipts; failed checks slash the bond and freeze rewards. A cedar reputation record preserves history, an ivory threshold limits cheap clones, and a spiral of fresh audits exposes coordinated identities before they gain control.
